name: Barbell Deadlift
movementPattern: Hip and knee extension - floor pull
grip: Double overhand, hands outside the legs. Mixed and hook grips are not illustrated.
description: Lift a barbell from a settled floor position by extending the hips and knees, keeping the bar close to the legs.
setup: Position the bar over the midfoot with feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge down and bend the knees to grasp the bar outside the legs.
Set a stable trunk, keep the arms long and take up tension against the bar before lifting.
instructions: Push through the floor and extend the hips and knees together while keeping the bar close.
Guide the bar past the knees without bending the elbows.
Stand tall with the bar at the thighs, without leaning backward.
Hinge back and bend the knees as needed to lower the bar, settle the plates and reset.
cues: Keep the bar near the legs.
commonMistakes: Jerking the bar from the floor with a rounded trunk.
Letting the hips rise far ahead of the shoulders or leaning back at lockout.

logging.example: A 20 kg bar plus two 15 kg plates: record 50 kg total.
logging.note: Include the bar and both sides' plates; preserve the original load convention in existing logs.

variantNote: Conventional floor-start stance, resetting each repetition. Sumo, trap-bar and Romanian deadlifts are separate variants.
reviewNotes: Plate diameter determines starting bar height; smaller plates may require a raised starting surface.
